items.a: No. LinkedIn OAuth is used for login, but profile information is not taken from the LinkedIn API. Users enter the summary, experience, education and skills into their own profiles themselves; this content is a form submitted to us, not an automatic pull.
items.q: Do you pull data from LinkedIn?

items.a: No. Audio and video flow directly between the two browsers over WebRTC; the server only carries the signaling (introduction) information. By default there is no recording feature and no media file is stored after the meeting.
A single set of commands: npm install, .env setup, npm run build and npm start. On average two minutes. Then you can open a room from the browser and share the invite link.
No. The entire flow works from the web app. The extension is a shortcut that makes it easier to open a room with one click while on LinkedIn and keep the interview panel open.
Yes. STUN is enough on most networks. For restricted networks like symmetric NAT, you can define your own TURN server in .env.
items.q: Can participants from different networks connect?

items.a: Both employers and candidates. Anyone who opens the invite link can join the room under their own name or with a LinkedIn login.

steps.title: Live interviews in three steps
steps: Connect with LinkedIn — Login is verified with LinkedIn OAuth. Profile data is not pulled from the LinkedIn API; you enter the information yourself.
Open a room and share the link — Send the room's invite link to the candidate through a LinkedIn message. No extra setup, no extra account, no download.
Interview and read the profile — When the candidate joins, video and profile come together. Share your screen, chat, and decide on one screen.
